name: Provide postpartum and newborn care
summary: After the birth, mother and baby stay together on the mother-baby unit for about one to three days. Postpartum nurses check the mother's recovery and the baby's feeding, weight and jaundice each shift, a lactation consultant helps with harder feeding problems, the newborn screening blood spot, bilirubin and hearing screens are done after 24 hours of age, a public health screen is completed, and the physicians or midwife write the discharge orders. Stays run long when discharge waits for morning rounds, a screen that cannot be done before 24 hours, a lactation consultant who works weekdays only, or phototherapy for jaundice.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 4,300 to 4,700 births a year and about 45 mother-baby beds.
baseline.notes: Unit of work is one mother-newborn stay on the mother-baby unit, from hand-over by the birthing unit to discharge home. Twins are counted as one stay.

trigger: The labour and delivery nurse hands over the mother and baby (or the mother alone when the baby is in the NICU) to the mother-baby unit.
end_state: Mother and baby leave the hospital with discharge teaching, follow-up arranged, the newborn screening card sent to Newborn Screening Ontario and the public health screen shared.

volume.seasonality: Follows births: slightly higher July to October. Discharges bunch on weekday late mornings after rounds.

evidence.note: One stay per birth: 4,690 babies born in 2021/22 and 4,277 in 2020/21; the low is the organisation file's 2018/19 figure.
Mother-baby nursing at about 1 nurse to 3 or 4 couplets around the clock on 45 beds gives roughly 12 to 15 nurses a shift; about 38 FTE of the 100 headcount (many part-time).
Weekday lactation consultants covering three sites; most of their time is on the mother-baby units.
Newborn examination and discharge for about half of babies, on morning rounds.
Family physicians round on their own patients' mothers and babies (about a third of stays).
Daily postpartum rounds and discharge orders for obstetrical patients, especially after caesarean.
Midwives see their clients (about a fifth) in hospital and usually discharge them early with home visits.
Unit clerks process transfers and discharges, send screening cards and fax summaries.
Infant Hearing Program screeners screen in hospital before discharge, mainly on day and evening shifts; cost is an estimate on the organisation file's 1.35 loading basis.

systems.name: Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Electronic bed board and patient flow dashboard
Fax (referrals, requisitions and reports to community physicians)
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones

steps.name: Receive hand-over and admit mother and baby
steps.description: The postpartum nurse takes report from the labour nurse, checks that mother and baby identification bands match, does a first assessment of both (vital signs, uterus, bleeding, pain; baby's colour, temperature, breathing) and orients the family to the room and infant security rules.

error.defect_description: Band mismatch or missed risk from the hand-over.

control.basis: Infant security and identification policy: match bands at every transfer

evidence.note: Admission tasks from general knowledge of Ontario mother-baby units; the wait is for a nurse busy with other couplets.

steps.name: Process the transfer in the information system
steps.description: The unit clerk moves the mother and newborn encounters to the mother-baby bed in the hospital information system, updates the bed board and prepares the paper forms the unit still uses (screening card, consent forms).

evidence.note: Caesarean share of 31% from the 31.7% Canadian rate in 2021-2022 (cihi_stays); clerk tasks from general knowledge.

steps.name: Give routine postpartum and newborn care each shift
steps.description: Across the stay the nurse checks the mother's vital signs, uterus, bleeding, perineum, bladder and pain, and the baby's temperature, breathing, feeds, wet and dirty diapers and weight, gives medications and charts each assessment in the hospital information system.

error.defect_description: Early sign of infection, hypoglycaemia or excess weight loss missed.

evidence.note: About 15 to 25 minutes per couplet per shift over four to six shifts; author's estimate.

steps.name: Give post-caesarean recovery care
steps.description: For a caesarean mother the nurse also manages the wound, urinary catheter removal, intravenous fluids and pain control, helps her get up and walk, gives blood-clot prevention and watches for bleeding and infection, while doing the routine newborn checks.

error.defect_description: Wound or urinary retention problem noticed late.

evidence.note: Additional post-operative nursing over two to three days; author's estimate.

steps.name: Support infant feeding
steps.description: The nurse watches feeds, helps with latch and positioning, teaches hand expression, and when supplements are needed explains options and records volumes. Babies who feed poorly or lose too much weight are referred to the lactation consultant.

evidence.note: Shares of babies under paediatricians, family physicians and midwives and the lactation referral rate are the author's estimates for an Ontario community hospital.

steps.name: Assess feeding with the lactation consultant
steps.description: The lactation consultant reviews the feeding chart and weight loss, watches a full feed, assesses latch, milk transfer and tongue movement, and writes a feeding plan with the parents. Consultants work weekdays, so a referral made on Friday evening waits for Monday or is handled by the nurses.

evidence.note: Lactation consultant assessment time and weekday availability from general knowledge of Ontario hospitals.

steps.name: Examine the newborn (paediatrician)
steps.description: On morning rounds the paediatrician reviews the chart, birth history and feeding, examines the baby head to toe (heart, hips, eyes, palate), reviews jaundice and blood sugar results and writes orders. Babies born in the evening are seen the next morning.

control.basis: Hospital medical staff rules: physician or midwife newborn examination before discharge

evidence.note: A physician newborn examination within 24 hours on daily rounds is standard practice; timing estimated.

steps.name: Examine mother and baby on rounds (family physician)
steps.description: The family physician visits before or after office hours, examines the mother and the baby, reviews feeding, bleeding and test results, and writes orders for both. Office schedules make the visit time hard to predict.

control.basis: Hospital medical staff rules: physician or midwife newborn examination before discharge

evidence.note: Family physician rounding pattern from general knowledge of Ontario community hospitals.

steps.name: Examine mother and baby and plan early discharge (midwife)
steps.description: The midwife examines her client and the baby, reviews feeding, and usually plans discharge within the first day with home visits; she may do the newborn screen and bilirubin herself at the home visit if the family leaves before 24 hours.

control.basis: Midwifery Act and hospital privileges: midwife is most responsible provider for her clients

next.condition: leaves before 24 hours with home follow-up

evidence.note: Ontario midwives provide postnatal home visits and often discharge clients early; shares estimated.

steps.name: Collect newborn screening blood spot and bilirubin
steps.description: Once the baby is 24 hours old the nurse warms the heel, collects drops onto the Newborn Screening Ontario card and a tube for total serum bilirubin from the same poke, checks the card details against the bands, and also does the pulse oximetry screen for critical heart disease. If parents decline, a refusal form is signed.

error.defect_description: Card filled incompletely, sample insufficient or taken before 24 hours, needing a repeat.

control.basis: Newborn Screening Ontario program: screening sample at 24 to 48 hours with informed refusal documented

evidence.note: Sample at 24 to 48 hours (nso_dbs); timed bilirubin drawn with the metabolic screen under the 2007 CPS approach in force in 2019-2022 (cps_bili). Pulse oximetry screening is from the author's knowledge. The wait is for the baby to reach 24 hours of age.

steps.name: Send the screening card to Newborn Screening Ontario
steps.description: The unit clerk logs the dried card in the unit's courier log and puts it in the daily courier pack to Newborn Screening Ontario in Ottawa. The card leaves after the family may already have gone home, so this step does not hold the stay.

evidence.note: Samples sent by courier from across the province (nso_dbs); daily courier and log are the author's knowledge.

steps.name: Plot the bilirubin and decide on treatment
steps.description: When the result comes back from the laboratory the nurse plots it by the baby's age in hours on the risk nomogram and calls the physician for babies in the higher-risk zones, who orders phototherapy or a repeat test.

error.defect_description: Plotted against the wrong age in hours.

evidence.note: Nomogram-guided follow-up of timed bilirubin under the 2007 approach (cps_bili); phototherapy rate of about 5% to 10% is the author's estimate. Wait is laboratory turnaround.

steps.name: Screen the baby's hearing
steps.description: The Infant Hearing Program screener brings the screening equipment to the room, tests each ear while the baby sleeps, enters the pass or refer result, and books an outpatient rescreen for babies who refer.

error.defect_description: Baby discharged before screening and not booked for outpatient screening.

evidence.note: Most babies are screened before hospital discharge (nygh_home); daytime screener schedule and times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Complete the public health postpartum screen
steps.description: The nurse asks the mother the Healthy Babies Healthy Children screening questions (social support, mood, feeding, finances), records consent and answers in the BORN Information System so the local public health unit can call the family.

error.defect_description: Screen skipped or incomplete when discharge is rushed.

control.basis: Healthy Babies Healthy Children program: postpartum screen offered with informed consent

evidence.note: Screening data shared from hospitals to public health through the BORN Information System, with consent (born_hbhc); interview time estimated.

steps.name: Write the maternal discharge order
steps.description: On rounds the obstetrician (or family physician) reviews the mother's bleeding, blood count, wound and pain, confirms she is ready, writes the discharge order, prescriptions and follow-up instructions, and dictates or types the discharge summary.

control.basis: Public Hospitals Act: discharge on the order of the attending physician or midwife

evidence.note: Discharge orders are written on morning rounds; a mother who is ready in the evening waits for the next morning. Times estimated.

steps.name: Write the newborn discharge order
steps.description: The baby's physician or midwife checks the weight loss, feeding, bilirubin zone, screening status and hearing result, writes the newborn discharge order and arranges a follow-up visit within two to three days.

control.basis: Public Hospitals Act: discharge on the order of the attending physician or midwife

evidence.note: Baby to see a care provider within two to three days of going home (nygh_home); family physicians and midwives sign for their own patients (see assumptions).

steps.name: Teach the family and check the car seat
steps.description: The nurse goes through discharge teaching: feeding and signs of enough intake, jaundice, safe sleep, bleeding and infection warning signs, postpartum mood, and when to call; checks the baby is buckled correctly in the car seat, removes the security tag and gives the written instructions.

error.defect_description: Teaching rushed at peak discharge time; family unsure when to seek help.

control.basis: Infant security system: tag removed only at discharge with band check

evidence.note: Follow-up timing told to families (public health call in two to three days, baby visit in two to three days) from nygh_home; teaching content and time are the author's knowledge.

steps.name: Complete discharge and send the summary
steps.description: The unit clerk discharges both encounters in the hospital information system so the bed shows as dirty on the bed board, faxes the discharge summaries to the family physician or paediatrician and files the paper forms for scanning.

error.defect_description: Summary faxed to the wrong or an outdated physician number.

evidence.note: Fax was the usual channel to community physicians in 2019-2022; author's knowledge.

steps.name: Review the caesarean mother on day two
steps.description: On the second post-operative day the nurse and obstetrician check the wound, removal of the dressing, bowel and bladder function and pain on oral medication before planning discharge.

evidence.note: Caesarean stays average 2.7 days versus 2.1 for all births (cihi_stays) and last at least 36 hours (nygh_home); elapsed time is recovery, not a queue.

steps.name: Give phototherapy and repeat the bilirubin
steps.description: The nurse places the baby under phototherapy lights with eye shields, keeps feeding on schedule, checks temperature and hydration, and repeats the bilirubin after the ordered interval; the stay usually extends by a day.

evidence.note: Phototherapy nursing and the wait for a phototherapy unit are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Check the repeat bilirubin after phototherapy
steps.description: After 12 to 24 hours of lights the nurse sends the repeat bilirubin and the physician decides whether to stop phototherapy and allow discharge.

evidence.note: Elapsed time is the treatment duration under the lights, not a queue; author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Jaundice needing phototherapy
exceptions.description: The timed bilirubin is in a high-risk zone; the baby has phototherapy and a repeat test, and the stay extends by about a day.

exceptions.name: Feeding problem
exceptions.description: Poor latch or high weight loss leads to a lactation consultant referral, which waits for a weekday.

exceptions.name: Midwifery early discharge
exceptions.description: A midwifery client goes home before 24 hours; the midwife does the newborn screen and bilirubin at a home visit.

exceptions.name: Repeat newborn screen
exceptions.description: Newborn Screening Ontario asks for a repeat sample because the card was taken too early or the spots were insufficient.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from arrival on the mother-baby unit to discharge

evidence.note: Whole birth stays average 2.1 days and caesarean stays 2.7 days in Canada (cihi_stays), of which about half a day is in the birthing unit; an Ontario hospital discharges about 24 hours after a vaginal birth and at least 36 hours after a caesarean (nygh_home). The p50 and p90 are the author's derivation from these.

pain_points.description: Discharge waits for physician rounds the next morning even when mother and baby are ready in the evening, and discharges bunch at late morning when nurses are busiest with teaching.

evidence.note: Author's knowledge of Ontario mother-baby unit flow.

pain_points.description: Newborn screening and bilirubin cannot be done before 24 hours of age, so a family ready to go earlier either waits or needs a return visit or midwife home visit.

evidence.note: Optimal sampling window 24 to 48 hours (nso_dbs).

pain_points.description: Lactation consultants work weekdays, so feeding problems found on weekends wait or fall to busy nurses.

evidence.note: Author's knowledge of hospital lactation staffing.

pain_points.description: The same information is entered in the hospital chart, the BORN system and paper screening cards, and discharge summaries are faxed.

evidence.note: Paper card by courier (nso_dbs) and BORN entry for public health (born_hbhc); fax and double entry from the author's knowledge.

sources.title: Halton Healthcare 2021-2022 Annual Community Report (By the Numbers)
sources.supports: 2021/22: 4,690 babies born; 161,049 emergency department visits; 37,964 dialysis visits; 62,508 mental health and addictions ambulatory visits; 5,228 staff.

sources.title: Halton Healthcare 2020-2021 Annual Community Report (By the Numbers)
sources.supports: 2020/21: 4,277 babies born; 126,357 emergency department visits; 37,171 dialysis visits; 89,823 addictions and mental health visits; top five in Ontario for patients on home dialysis (Ontario Renal Network, March 2021).

sources.title: Hospital stays in Canada, 2021-2022
sources.supports: Giving birth was the most common reason for hospitalization, average acute stay 2.1 days; caesarean section the most common inpatient surgery, average stay 2.7 days; total caesarean rate 31.7% in 2021-2022, up from 28.8% in 2017-2018.

sources.title: Dried Blood Spot Screening
sources.supports: The optimal time for newborn screening is 24 to 48 hours after birth; the sample is taken from the baby's heel onto a newborn screening card; samples are sent to Newborn Screening Ontario by courier; results go to the ordering provider at the birth hospital or midwifery practice.

sources.title: Guidelines for detection and management of hyperbilirubinemia in term and late preterm newborns (E. Ng et al., CPS Fetus and Newborn Committee)
sources.supports: Replaces the 2007 CPS statement, under which all healthy newborns were screened with a timed total serum bilirubin between 18 and 72 hours of age and a nomogram guided follow-up; the bilirubin can be drawn at the same time as the newborn metabolic screen.

sources.title: Going Home (maternal newborn care after delivery)
sources.supports: Ontario community teaching hospital: discharge about 24 hours after an uncomplicated vaginal birth, at least 36 hours after a caesarean; most babies have a hearing screen before discharge; a public health nurse calls within two to three days; baby to see a care provider within two to three days.

sources.title: Healthy Babies Healthy Children Program
sources.supports: Maternal-child screening data are shared electronically between hospitals and public health units through the BORN Information System; participation is optional and based on informed consent; public health nurses contact eligible families within 48 hours of hospital discharge.

assumptions: Describes the common practice of an Ontario community hospital mother-baby unit in 2019-2022, not Halton Healthcare's own procedures.

The hearing screen is done by an Infant Hearing Program screener (added as hearing_screener, not in the organisation file). The organisation file also lacks the link from labour and delivery for a mother whose baby is in the NICU (maternity_patient) and lists no cleaning request to environmental cleaning at discharge.

The bilirubin approach is the 2007 Canadian Paediatric Society one in force during 2019-2022 (timed serum bilirubin between 18 and 72 hours plotted on a nomogram), as described in the 2025 statement that replaced it.

Step s15 uses the obstetrician role and s16 the paediatrician role; family physicians sign both orders for their own patients and midwives for their clients, so physician cost is somewhat overstated in these steps.
The bed resource is held for the whole stay and recorded on the admission step (s01).
Provider shares (paediatrician 43%, family physician 20%, midwife 15% of babies), feeding referral (22%), phototherapy (8%) and midwifery early discharge are tier C estimates.
The organisation file links NICU babies back to this process (wc-nicu-care newborn); these are counted as 3% of stays when a baby rejoins the mother before discharge.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage times 1.35); the hearing screener cost is an estimate on the same basis.

Postpartum nurse FTE (38) is set by around-the-clock ratio staffing of about one nurse to three or four couplets; the simulated hands-on minutes imply about a third of that, because nurses also spend unmeasured time on call bells, rounds, breaks and empty beds.

At 360 stays a month and a median stay of about 1.5 days the unit needs about 18 to 20 occupied beds on average, or about 23 to 25 beds at 80% occupancy. The organisation file's 45 mother-baby beds would run at about 40% occupancy, so its bed count probably includes antepartum, gynaecology or paediatric beds.
